body:
Measured cold from the published 0.3.0: loam init mints exactly operator.seed and config.json. No user (so /login is a door with nobody to be), no schemas (a virgin store has NO queryable surface). The real onboarding is seven commands, and the two a newcomer cannot guess - user create and the five stock registers - are the ones init omits. Myk's order, 2026-08-27: init finishes the job.

THE RULES (Myk's, refined against the frozen-rail reality):
- In the GUIDED flow the initial user NAME is never invented: it arrives via --user <name> or an interactive TTY prompt, nothing else. The password arrives via the TTY prompt (twice, echo off) or --password-file <path> for non-interactive use - never a bare flag (shell history).
- Skipping is always EXPLICIT: --no-user skips user creation (with a printed note that /login stays dark until loam user create); --no-stock skips the shelf; --stock <name,...|all> selects (default all).
- A flagless NON-TTY init keeps today's bare behavior byte-for-byte - scripts and the many frozen rails calling run(["init"]) are untouched. Any guided flag, or a TTY, enters the guided flow.
- The guided flow ends by printing the next step: the serve command and the login URL shape.

Build: cmdInit grows the flow; user creation reuses the existing user-create implementation (readSecret already exists for embedders); the stock loop is the T244 install machinery (transitive deps pull shallow-person). Everything runs server-down by construction - init precedes serve - so the T243 staleness trap cannot fire.

Acceptance criteria: working spec at .adlc/specs/54-guided-init.md, each naming its rail.

Merge tier: new CLI behavior on the published surface - Myk merges.
title: loam init finishes the job - a guided first run from npm i to a living store
